title: Document conversion: docling and its local alternatives, scopes B and C

corpora.label: scope B
corpora.description: security procedures of a manufacturing company (PDF, scans, Office)
corpora.formats: text PDFs, scanned PDFs, Word, Excel, slide decks of training courses with speaker notes
corpora.sample: 15 files: 7 PDFs (2 of them scanned), 1 .doc, 2 spreadsheets, 5 slide decks

corpora.label: scope C
corpora.description: machine manuals (Word, many languages and scripts)
corpora.sample: 9 manuals in Italian, English, Chinese, Arabic, Russian, Greek and Korean (.doc and .docx); PDFs made with LibreOffice

pages.by_kind: B: 5 scanned pages, 9 pages of text PDFs (tables, wide tables, an index), 3 slides, 1 page of a .doc; C: 12 pages of manuals (Latin, CJK, Arabic, Cyrillic, Greek, Korean scripts)
pages.reference: a transcription by Claude Opus reading the page image, with fixed rules: headings at their levels, tables in markdown (HTML when cells are merged), a [figure] placeholder where each image sits, page headers and footers left out. 7-21 s and about 11,000 tokens a page; five pages are being checked by hand, until then the reference is a model's reading
pages.whole_documents: 444 PDF pages and 402 pages of original files, for the timings; the 3 whole .docx manuals against a quasi-reference read from the Word file itself (python-docx)

gpu_host.use: every model: embeddings, reranker, answers, judges, image descriptions, OCR models
gpu_host.rule: everything stays in the 16 GB of VRAM, nothing offloaded to the CPU

cpu_host.use: gosidian, the plugins, Qdrant and PostgreSQL, the converters that run on the CPU

software.containers: each CPU tool in a throwaway container without network, 6 CPUs and 12 GB (MinerU 16 GB); GPU models one at a time on vLLM

metrics.text: 1 - normalized character edit distance (markup removed, spaces collapsed, case kept)
metrics.headings: F1 of the headings matched by similar text (0.8 or more)
metrics.levels: matched headings at the same relative level
metrics.order: pairs of blocks in the reference's order (normalized Kendall)
metrics.tables: F1 on the cells (row, column, similar text); merged cells expanded; a table not recognized loses its cells
metrics.structure: reference tables matched with the same number of rows and columns
metrics.images_n: ratio of the number of images (min/max, per page)
metrics.images_pos: reference images with an image of the tool after the same block (one block of tolerance)
metrics.clean: 1 - share of the page header and footer lines left in the text
metrics.notes: share of the slides with speaker notes whose text is in the output
metrics.cells / content: F1 on (row, column, text) of the sheet / share of the sheet's values found in any table
metrics.native: the tool converted the original file; measured on the stretch of the document that matches the page

notes: values from 0 to 1, 1 = as the reference; no overall score: the winner is picked format by format, as the pipeline will
the image descriptions are out of this benchmark: they are a step of the pipeline (llm.describe_media), the same for every converter
GPU times: one page at a time; on whole PDFs, in batches, the GPU models take 1.1-1.6 s a page. PaddleOCR-VL spends 5 s of its 7.7 on the layout model, on the CPU
Claude against the quasi-reference of the 3 whole Word manuals (independent of Claude): text 0.90, tables 0.70; the native readers 0.98-0.99 and 0.91-0.99
a small invention seen once from Claude: a header row added to a table that has none
docling 0.5.0 picture_text: the page of pictograms C-10 goes from 0.06 to 0.79 of text, all 18 labels present; Arabic from the PDF loses a little

choice.what: docling 0.5.0 stays the default converter, with office: auto and picture_text; for scans and hard PDFs a small OCR vision model is the candidate for a second plugin (open)
choice.why: Word: the native readers beat the PDF route (text 0.99 against 0.64 on whole manuals, images in place) and even a hosted model; scans: dots.ocr, PaddleOCR-VL and GLM-OCR read 0.98-0.99 of the text against 0.89 of docling with OCR; text PDFs: PaddleOCR-VL, MinerU VLM, GLM-OCR and OvisOCR2 get the tables right (1.00 against 0.88); slides: only docling and MarkItDown keep the speaker notes
